versions.short: The bill would require the Federal Communications Commission, after consulting other agencies, to set up a taskforce within 270 days to study how to combat unlawful robocalls coming into the United States from abroad and report its recommendations to Congress within 360 days of its creation. It would also let the Commission require some voice service providers to post a bond of up to $100,000 before filing certifications in the Robocall Mitigation Database, with exemptions for established, regulated providers. In addition, it would give immunity from lawsuits to the registered consortium that receives, shares, or publishes trace back information about suspected illegal robocalls, and allow the Commission to publish a list of providers that refuse to take part in trace back efforts or that carry substantial amounts of unlawful robocalls.
